- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3), model underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing sharp drops.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +10%+ above 70) — cap forecast overshoot at +5% of prior peak.
- After a sharp decline (e.g., -10%+ from prior day), model often fails to fully correct — add 2–5% lagged recovery bias to forecast.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show price >72, model tends to overpredict; apply downward correction of 2–4% per day.
- Sentiment volatility >0.3 SD from mean → reduce forecast horizon sensitivity; apply smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to noisy sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.6 → -0.4 → +0.5), model misreads momentum — adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing direction, not magnitude.
